name: Question 10
worked_solution:
The gradient of the function $f(x,y,z)$ is defined as

$$
∇f(x,y,z)=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\,i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\,j+\frac{∂f}{∂z}\,k.
$$

Since $∇f(x,y,z)=F(x,y,z),$ the function $f(x,y,z)$ must satisfy the following system:

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=y+1,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x+z+1,\,\frac{∂f}{∂z}=y+1
$$

First, we integrate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ with respect to $x.$ Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $y$ and $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =\int \frac{∂f}{∂x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (y+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =xy+x+g(y,z)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, differentiating the above expression with respect to $y,$ we obtain

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x+\frac{∂g}{∂y}
$$

Taking $\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x+z+1$ into account, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x+\frac{∂g}{∂y} & =x+z+1 \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =z+1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate $\frac{∂g}{∂y}$ with respect to $y.$ Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}g(y,z) & =\int \frac{∂g}{∂y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\int (z+1)\,\text{d}y \\  & =yz+y+h(z)\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $g(y,z)=yz+y+h(z)$ in the expression for $f(x,y,z),$ we get

$$
f(x,y,z)=xy+x+yz+y+h(z).
$$

To determine the function $h(z),$ we differentiate $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z.$ This gives

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂z}=y+{h}^{′}(z).
$$

Taking $\frac{∂f}{∂z}=y+1$ into account, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y+1 & =y+{h}^{′}(z) \\ {h}^{′}(z) & =1 \\ h(z) & =z+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is a constant.

Consequently,

$$
f(x,y,z)=xy+yz+x+y+z+C.
$$

Question 10
?

Find f(x,y,z) such that ∇f(x,y,z)=F(x,y,z), where F(x,y,z)=(y+1)i+(x+z+1)j+(y+1)k.

a
f(x,y,z)=xyz+x+y+z+C
b
f(x,y,z)=xy+yz+xz+x+y+C
c
f(x,y,z)=xy+yz+xz+y+z+C
d
f(x,y,z)=xyz+xz+xy+yz+C
e
f(x,y,z)=xy+yz+x+y+z+C
Don't Know
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The gradient of the function f(x,y,z) is defined as ∇f(x,y,z)=∂f∂xi+∂f∂yj+∂f∂zk.

Since ∇f(x,y,z)=F(x,y,z), the function f(x,y,z) must satisfy the following system: ∂f∂x=y+1,∂f∂y=x+z+1,∂f∂z=y+1

First, we integrate ∂f∂x with respect to x. Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of y and z: f(x,y,z)=∫∂f∂xdx=∫(y+1)dx=xy+x+g(y,z)

Now, differentiating the above expression with respect to y, we obtain ∂f∂y=x+∂g∂y

Taking ∂f∂y=x+z+1 into account, we obtain

x+∂g∂y=x+z+1∂g∂y=z+1

Now, we integrate ∂g∂y with respect to y. Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of z: g(y,z)=∫∂g∂ydy=∫(z+1)dy=yz+y+h(z)

Substituting g(y,z)=yz+y+h(z) in the expression for f(x,y,z), we get f(x,y,z)=xy+x+yz+y+h(z).

To determine the function h(z), we differentiate f(x,y,z) with respect to z. This gives ∂f∂z=y+h′(z).

Taking ∂f∂z=y+1 into account, we obtain y+1=y+h′(z)h′(z)=1h(z)=z+C, where C is a constant.

Consequently, f(x,y,z)=xy+yz+x+y+z+C.
